items.title: Section: Nine More Ways a Practitioner Falls, from Illness to a Beautiful Stranger's Face

items.zh: 謂如有一，遭極重病。如馬勝言：我於此定不能入證，將無我定當退失耶？或復有一，性多麁重，於三摩地先不串習，彼由如是多麁重故，成其退法。或有所緣境界勝故，從離欲退。謂如有一，值遇勝妙境界現前。如外道仙乃至獲得非想非非想處，遇觸少年美妙形色可愛母邑，從離欲退。或有獲得敬養故退。謂如有一，從他獲得利養恭敬，即便退墮。如提婆達多。或有遭遇輕毀故退。謂如有一，或遭他罵、或瞋、或責，從離欲退。如外道仙，由憤恚故退三摩地，現行呪詛。或慢故退。謂如有一，恃所得定自舉凌他。或有增上慢故退。謂如有一，於諸勝定證差別中，起增上慢。或有不作意故退。謂如有一，於能入定行相作意不復思惟。或有未串習故退。謂如有一，安住始業新修善品。或有自地煩惱數起故退。謂如有一，愛上靜慮乃至疑上靜慮。或有壽盡、福盡、業盡故退。謂如有一，從上生處退沒下生。
items.en: As when one afflicted by a grave illness, like Aśvajit, finds this concentration cannot be entered and wonders whether it is about to be lost. As when one encounters a supremely alluring object present before them. As when one falls upon receiving honour and support from another, as with Devadatta. As when one falls back because a lifespan, merit, or karma has run its course, one born in a higher realm falling back down to a lower one.

items.title: Section: Four Kinds of Practitioner, and Two Ways of Leaving Absorption

items.zh: 復次，此中或有補特伽羅，下品煩惱、下品善法，多念艱辛然後方退，多念艱辛方能入定。或有補特伽羅，下品煩惱、上品善法，多念艱辛然後方退，經一念頃速能入定。或有補特伽羅，上品煩惱、下品善法，經一念頃速疾而退，多念艱辛方能入定。或有補特伽羅，上品煩惱、上品善法，經一剎那速疾而退，一剎那頃速能入定。復有補特伽羅已得離欲，從定起已，或於一時，彼三摩地相間相雜作意而轉；或於一時，不相間雜。
items.en: There is a kind of person with minor affliction and minor wholesome quality, hard to lose yet hard to enter. There is a kind with minor affliction and excellent wholesome quality, hard to lose yet swift to enter. There is a kind with strong affliction and minor wholesome quality, swift to lose yet hard to enter. There is a kind with strong affliction and excellent wholesome quality, swift to lose and swift to enter alike. There is also a person already free of desire who, having emerged from concentration, at times engages in activity of mind interspersed and mixed with that same concentration, and at times engages in activity of mind not so intermixed.

items.zh: 若遇聲緣，從定而起，與定相應意識俱轉，餘耳識生，非即彼定相應意識能取此聲。若不爾者，於此音聲不領受故，不應出定。非取聲時即便出定。領受聲已，若有悕望後時方出。

items.title: Section: Hearing Thunder in Absorption, and the Ground of Meditative Equipoise Comes to Its Own Close

items.zh: 於此地中餘決擇文，更不復現。如是已說三摩呬多地決擇。非三摩呬多決擇，我今當說。或有由自性故，名不定地。謂五識身。或有闕輕安故，名不定地。謂在欲界諸心心法。或有未發趣故，名不定地。謂受欲者。或有散亂故，名不定地。謂始業者雖修習定，而於五欲其心流散。
items.en: The remaining decisive-discernment texts on this ground will not appear again. The decisive discernment of the Ground of Non-Meditative-Equipoise, within the chapter of decisive discernment. Thus I have already explained the decisive discernment of the Ground of Meditative Equipoise. I shall now explain the decisive discernment of the Ground of Non-Meditative-Equipoise. Some are called non-concentrated through their own nature, namely the five sense consciousnesses. Some are called non-concentrated through lacking pliancy, namely mental states bound to the desire realm. Some are called non-concentrated through never having set out towards it, namely those who enjoy desires. Some are called non-concentrated through scatteredness, namely a beginning practitioner whose mind, though cultivating concentration, still flows towards the five desires.

items.title: Section: Twelve Ways of Falling Short of Genuine Concentration

items.zh: 或有太聚故，名不定地。謂始業者，於內境界略聚其心，便生沈沒。或未得故，名不定地。謂即散心相應諸法。或未圓滿故，名不定地。謂未證得加行究竟作意。或雜染故，名不定地。謂雖證得加行究竟果作意，而於彼定多生愛味。或不自在故，名不定地。謂即由彼染污心故，不得自在。或不清淨故，名不定地。謂未永害煩惱隨眠。或出定故，名不定地。謂從已得三摩地起而不退失。或有退故，名不定地。謂從所得三摩地退。
items.en: Some are non-concentrated through being overly contracted, a beginner's mind, narrowed too far, falling into dullness. Some through not yet having attained it, mental states still associated with scattering. Some through incompleteness, not yet having attained the application-perfecting attention. Some through defilement, craving arising towards the concentration attained. Some through lacking mastery, this defiled mind preventing free entry and exit. Some through impurity, the underlying tendencies not yet permanently destroyed. Some simply through being presently outside concentration, though not lost. And some through having genuinely fallen back from concentration once attained.

blocks.text: How meditators fall back, and a famous question: can someone in deep absorption hear thunder?

Master Cháng Bǎi: "I am so ill I cannot enter the absorption I attained." Receiving respect and gain, a practitioner grows greedy and falls; the treatise names Devadatta. From a higher birth, when life ends, one falls back to a lower one.

Master Cháng Bǎi: with light afflictions, one falls only after much difficulty; with excellent wholesome qualities, one enters in a moment; with heavy afflictions, one falls easily; with weak qualities, entry is hard.

(Untranslated, 0650c20: hearing a sound, one emerges: mental consciousness joined with the absorption continues, and a separate ear-consciousness arises; one does not emerge at the very moment of hearing, but afterwards, if one wishes.) Master Cháng Bǎi: the five consciousnesses rely on outer objects and flow outward; meditation gathers the mind inward.

Master Cháng Bǎi: some have no intention to attain concentration; some practise, but the mind still scatters. Some attain root absorption and crave it. An object too small invites dullness and sleep. Even one with concentration may lose it if the seeds of affliction remain.
"One does not emerge the instant one hears." The treatise describes absorption precisely, as something with its own momentum.

quiz.q: This is rendered "wonders whether this concentration cannot be entered because it has already been lost." What is reversed?
options: nothing: Aśvajit has already lost it and doubts only his entry, as the lecture explains
not entering is a fact and falling away a future fear, whereas the English takes loss as the past cause
馬勝 should be "Mahākāśyapa"
定 should be "precepts"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "I am so ill that I cannot enter the absorption I attained; might my concentration fall away?" Not entering is what is happening now, and loss is the worry. The English makes loss the prior cause.

quiz.q: What kind of falling back does the treatise illustrate with Devadatta?
options: falling through a supremely alluring object present before one
falling through the end of lifespan
falling through receiving honour and support
falling through the imbalance of the elements
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: receiving respect and gain, a practitioner grows greedy and falls from freedom from desire. The treatise names Devadatta for this case. Illness is the case of Aśvajit, and an alluring object is another case.

quiz.q: What is the case of falling through the end of lifespan, merit, or karma?
options: falling from a higher place of birth down to a lower one
leaving absorption for a scattered mind, one's power spent, unrelated to rebirth
falling from a noble fruit to ordinary status
falling from monk to layperson
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: from a higher place of birth, such as the form or formless heavens, when life ends one falls away and is born below. This falling concerns rebirth, the last of the ten, while the English omits six in between.

quiz.q: What is the case with minor affliction and excellent wholesome quality?
options: swift to lose, hard to enter, excellent quality being easily shaken
hard to lose, yet swift to enter
hard to lose, hard to enter
swift to lose, swift to enter
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: with excellent wholesome quality, wishing to enter concentration, one enters in a moment. With light afflictions, one falls only after hard moments. This combination is the most favourable of the four, though the treatise itself makes no ranking.

quiz.q: What is the case with strong affliction and minor wholesome quality?
options: hard to lose, swift to enter, strong affliction matching strong concentration
swift to lose, yet hard to enter
swift to lose, swift to enter
hard to lose, hard to enter
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: with strong afflictions, as soon as one arises one falls from absorption; with minor wholesome quality, entering is very hard. Both tendencies run against the practitioner here, which sets this case apart from the other three.

quiz.q: What general rule does Master Cháng Bǎi draw from the four cases?
options: heavy afflictions fall easily and light ones with difficulty; excellent practice enters easily and poor practice with difficulty
heavy affliction enters fast, and wholesome quality decides only falling
the old fall easily, the young with difficulty
monastics fall with difficulty, householders easily
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: those with heavy affliction fall easily, and those with light affliction hardly at all; excellent calm and insight enters easily, and inferior practice with difficulty. Affliction governs falling and practice governs entering.

quiz.q: Why are the five sense consciousnesses non-concentrated through their own nature?
options: they are afflictions by nature and must first be cut before meditation
they rely on outer objects and flow outward, and only the sixth consciousness can gather and focus
they are too subtle to notice
only arhats have them
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the five consciousnesses rise only by relying on outer objects, cannot arise repeatedly at will, and flow outward; meditation requires gathering and focusing, and only the sixth consciousness can do this.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain desire-realm mental states lacking pliancy?
options: the desire realm has no one-pointedness at all, not even a moment's focus
only arhats have pliancy
the desire realm has one-pointedness, but no pliancy nourishing body and mind, so it is not a ground of concentration
pliancy is bodily health
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: pliancy exists only from threshold concentration upwards; desire-realm mental states may have some one-pointedness and a desire-realm concentration, but no pliant bliss soaks body and mind, so they are not called a ground of concentration.

quiz.q: How do non-concentration through not setting out and through scatteredness differ?
options: not setting out is a beginner, while only one with concentration can be scattered
both mean one who has fallen back
not setting out is one enjoying desires; scatteredness is a beginner meditating with a mind flowing towards them
both mean the five consciousnesses
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: not setting out means having no intention or vow to attain concentration; scatteredness means one practices absorption but the mind still cannot leave the five desires. One has not begun, and the other has begun without yet settling.

quiz.q: This is rendered "craving arising towards the concentration attained." What is lost?
options: nothing: the premise is implied, the two cases being the same, as the lecture sees
愛 is lost
定 is lost
雖證得加行究竟果作意, the premise dividing incompleteness from defilement
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: though one has achieved the fruit of completed application and attained root absorption, one craves it. The preceding case had not attained it. Without this premise, the English does not show how the two cases differ.

quiz.q: Why is being overly contracted non-concentrated?
options: objects are too many, the mind running after them, the same as scatteredness in effect
the body sits too tensely
the object is too small, the mind cannot stay focused, and dullness and sleep arise
there is too much company
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the mind's object is too small, one cannot stay focused on so slight an object, and dullness and sleep arise, obstructing concentration. It is the opposite failure to scatteredness, a mind drawn too far in.

quiz.q: What does non-concentration through impurity refer to?
options: broken precepts, as impure morality prevents concentration
an unclean body
an impure dwelling
the underlying tendencies not yet permanently destroyed
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: this means the seeds of affliction are not completely cut, so afflictions may still arise and absorption may be lost. Thus even one with concentration can be called non-concentrated in this respect.
